cross_document_findings.boundary: The number of opposition documents in this publisher family is not a statistically representative measure of community opinion.
cross_document_findings.finding: Planning support and public opposition coexist in the preserved record.

cross_document_findings.boundary: The documents do not establish that public comments caused the added condition.
cross_document_findings.finding: The March 9 substitute adds an operating-hours condition to the seven-condition original ordinance.

cross_document_findings.boundary: Continued submissions establish continued expressed opposition by these writers, not community-wide consensus.
cross_document_findings.finding: Public opposition continued after the March 9 hearing date.

cross_document_findings.boundary: The request is not itself a final disposition and does not prove Council's reason for later TIME status.
cross_document_findings.finding: The applicant requested additional review time on March 30 to engage community/Council and explain the plan.

cross_document_findings.boundary: Image-only/handwritten material and referenced testimony/photos remain unresolved rather than inferred.
cross_document_findings.finding: The record family contains unresolved referenced evidence and representation gaps.

observations: Planning memorandum identifies PC-2025-80-CU and the residential/park/church context.
Planning Staff states the conditional use is consistent with Section 153.474 and the Land Use and Development Guide Plan and recommends approval.
Fact sheet states Planning Staff and Planning Commission recommended approval.
Original ordinance carries seven conditions, including archery fencing and a prohibition on live ammunition.
February 19 notice schedules March 9, 2026 Planning & Economic Development discussion and a 5:00 p.m. open-comment public hearing.
Notice provides in-person, remote, and written-comment participation routes.
Petition describes repurposing Eastwood Swim Park as a defense-education facility serving public, police, fire, and EMS.
Application states an estimated total project cost of $677,000.
Business materials describe phased uses including a configurable training structure, Simunition-based scenarios, archery, obstacle/K9 training, and a possible rappel tower.
Many later diagram/image pages are OCR-noisy; claims in petitioner materials remain applicant statements unless independently corroborated.
Bundle contains multiple pre-hearing comments opposing or questioning the location and land-use compatibility.
Recurring themes include residential/park compatibility, safety, noise, traffic/parking, property values, and impacts on nearby recreation.
Summit Metro Parks submission raises safety/noise/park-character concerns while recognizing first-responder training as a legitimate need.
Page 5 remains blank/unresolved after OCR and should not be inferred.
March 9 letter from Tallmadge Mayor Carol Siciliano-Kilway urges Akron Council to vote no.
Letter emphasizes cross-border residential impact, noise/activity/safety, traffic, and property-value concerns.
March 9 substitute preserves the original seven conditions and adds an eighth condition limiting operating hours to 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Monday-Saturday and 10 a.m.-6 p.m. Sunday.
The preserved text does not add explicit new conditions for a noise study, hard-surfaced parking, security, or property-value mitigation.
The existence/timing of the amendment is observable; the record does not establish which comments, if any, caused it.
OCR yields mostly screenshot/image noise.
Semantic content is not safely recoverable from the preserved text corpus; visual review remains an unresolved evidence task.
March 16 John and Luciana Rutecki submission argues incompatibility with U1 residential zoning and raises noise, parking, park-use, aesthetics, and property-value concerns.
Submission explicitly challenges Planning Staff's compatibility reasoning and proposes questions for Council.
March 16 letter signed by Tallmadge council members conveys resident concerns and questions compatibility with surrounding residential areas and the Land Use and Development Guide Plan.
Letter respects Akron's jurisdiction while asking Council to consider cross-community impacts.
Contains the same Tallmadge forwarding email seen in publish 102595 but omits the attached signed letter.
This is a useful example of byte-unique publisher artifacts containing semantically overlapping record content; provenance should be preserved even if later deduplicated for reading.
Email wrapper identifies a constituent communication associated with 1849 Eastwood Avenue.
Four handwritten/image pages remain too noisy for safe semantic normalization from OCR alone; detailed claims remain unresolved pending visual review.
March 16 forwarded objection argues the training facility is ill-suited to the neighborhood/Metro Park edge and suggests a different site.
Forwarded message objects to the Eastwood location and references perceived support by Ward 10 representation.
The writer's statement about another person's position is not independently treated as proof of that position.
First section opposes the Eastwood training proposal on safety/wildlife/park concerns.
Second section concerns an unrelated bitcoin/AI data-center allegation.
Document demonstrates why relevance should be segment-level rather than treating every statement in a linked document as part of the Eastwood matter.
March 18 Tallmadge resident opposes the location based on Metro Park, neighborhood, safety, and unanswered public-access questions.
March 18 Parkside Condos HOA president opposes the location and reports attending the hearing.
The writer reports that most hearing speakers opposed the project and describes one non-attorney supporter; those hearing-count observations remain witness statements, not a transcript.
March 20 Tallmadge-area writer raises business-model, user-access, security, noise, traffic, property-value, and public-safety questions.
Writer explicitly says the business plan should be refined before Council votes.
March 20 nearby resident opposes the location, references attending and speaking at the March 9 meeting, and reports signing a petition.
Writer's recollection of another attendee's statement remains testimony about the hearing, not independently verified transcript evidence.
March 23 Melissa Riley-Smith letter is the previously blind-audited document.
References prior March 9 testimony and photographs submitted at the meeting; those referenced photographs/testimony are not present in this two-page attachment.
Contains property-value estimates and the shorthand range $10,000-20,000 that exposed the earlier parser/anchor representation boundary.
Document directly proves the resident made these claims; it does not prove the predicted depreciation or environmental effects occurred.
March 30 applicant counsel formally requests additional time for review.
Stated reason is to refresh application status with the community and Council and more fully explain the proposed business model and plan.
Request establishes a procedural reason offered by the applicant for additional time; it does not prove why Council kept the matter under TIME.

outcome.reason: No document in the audited 20-document family establishes final passage, denial, withdrawal, or other terminal disposition.

procedural_chronology.event: Planning Commission review identified in official planning memorandum; staff/commission recommend approval.
Clerk issues notice for March 9 open-comment hearing.
Substitute ordinance dated/offered; preserved official agenda elsewhere in T21 explicitly records public hearing held and substitute offered.
Post-hearing opposition and cross-jurisdiction concerns continue in publisher attachments.
Additional constituent opposition is forwarded into the Council record.
Previously blind-audited resident letter is forwarded, referencing March 9 testimony/photos.
Applicant attorney requests additional time to explain/refine community and Council understanding of the business model.

unresolved_evidence_obligations.obligation: Locate or establish availability of March 9 hearing recording/transcript/minutes sufficient to attribute testimony directly.
Locate photographs Melissa Riley-Smith says she submitted at the March 9 meeting.
Visually inspect handwritten/image pages in publish 102597.
Trace final ordinance disposition beyond the April 27 family and repeated TIME agenda appearances.
